newsitem.title: USA: Cold causes widespread damage to Texas wheat.
newsitem.headline: Cold causes widespread damage to Texas wheat.

text.p: Extreme cold caused widespread damage to Texas wheat but the extent will not be known until a warmup occurs, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said Monday in its weekly crop report.

"The weather maker of the week was a very strong, unusually late cold front that moved rapidly across the state late in the week," the report said. "Most (wheat) fields were in the boot stage at the time of the frontal passage."
The front spawned heavy rains and tornadoes, and little fieldwork occurred during the week in most areas of the state.
Wheat was rated 61 percent good to excellent, up from 51 percent a week earlier. But that rating did not take into account the cold-related damage, which was unknown.
Texas corn condition was rated two percent excellent, 39 good, 47 fair, 11 poor and one very poor. Sorghum was rated one percent excellent, 59 good, 37 fair and three poor.
Cotton planting was slowly increasing in parts of central Texas, but cold, wet conditions kept progress to a minimum.
Texas range and pasture condition was rated 13 percent excellent, 48 good, 30 fair, eight poor and one very poor.
